description: The March 10 and March 17 reports establish separate intraparliamentary walkouts but provide no participant count. It is unresolved whether these legislative actions constitute public gatherings under MM and whether either reached 50 simultaneously.
required_followup: Seek distinct permitted reporting or official sitting records that establish attendance, public-gathering context and the precise demand; do not infer a count from party membership or Parliament size.

description: Both reports describe objections to parliamentary committee procedures, but the exposed text gives limited detail about the remedy demanded and whether the walkout was a public anti-state protest rather than a legislative tactic.
required_followup: If new permitted sources are found, document the explicit requested decision and whether it was directed to state institutions.

description: The two walkouts occurred on different dates within one week and concern committee formation, but no report explicitly links them. Keep them separate; relation remains a possible continuation only.
required_followup: Look for a contemporaneous account explicitly linking the March 10 and March 17 actions or describing a continuing opposition campaign; do not merge by shared actors/issue alone.

description: Open-web discovery included English local/national news and limited Setswana terms, four date-window prompts, Gaborone/Francistown/Palapye searches, parliament/political process and labor-sector prompts. Search results were pooled and date filtering was not verified. No systematic print/archive or LexisNexis coverage, and no fully verified Setswana corpus was available.
required_followup: Use any needed distinct local/regional sources to assess event validity and other regions/sectors. Avoid exhaustive or zero-protest claims.
